_comment: Tunable Phase 2 visual language for Cloudreach. It deliberately reuses the Meadows terrain textures and generated ground-cover meshes: one nature family, a different high-altitude composition.

sky_profile._comment: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C4). The blind judge read every Cloudreach frame as 'the same flat cyan gradient with thin wisps ... no cumulus mass, no cloud below eye level' and called the region's name a lie. That was authored here, not a shader limit: this profile is merged over EVERY art.json time-of-day preset (cloudreach_world.gd::merge_sky_profile_into_times), and it was flattening the shipped Meadows sky rather than dressing it -- cloud_lit_contrast 0.10 against art.json's own 6.0 is what turns a lit cumulus into a wisp, and cloud_sun_gain 0.35 against 1.1 removes the sunward brightening that gives a cloud a top and a base. Every key below maps 1:1 onto a shaders/sky_clouds.gdshader uniform through world_look.gd::_apply_cloud_sky; deleting a key falls back to art.json's Meadows value, and deleting the block falls back to the Meadows sky entire. Colours are deliberately NOT set here: this profile is merged into the night and dawn presets too, and a fixed cloud_lit/cloud_shade would light the night sky like noon.
sky_profile._comment_energy: The blind judge measured this realm's frames at p90 121-138 / p99 147-170 against the key art's 191/231 and palworld-02's 209/223, at 10-18 points MORE saturation -- saturated and dark at once, which is what reads as muddy however vivid the hue is. It also found the two headline cliff masses sampling near black on every face away from the sun. `energy` is the sky dome's own multiplier, and scenes/world/cloudreach_cliffs.tscn runs ambient_light_sky_contribution 0.52, so raising it lifts the sky AND the ambient fill that is the only light a shadowed cliff face gets here. Scoped to this realm's profile on purpose: art.json's global sky drives the Meadows too.
sky_profile._comment_round2: Round 2, measured off the round-1 render rather than guessed: coverage 0.55 with sharpness 2.9, high_coverage 0.38 and haze_strength 0.66 did not read as massed cumulus over blue, it read as total overcast -- the sky went near-white and the only blue left was the gaps BETWEEN clouds. Cut coverage and the cirrus layer, put sharpness back above art.json's own 3.4 so a cloud has an edge instead of bleeding into its neighbour, and lifted cloud_altitude so the deck sits higher on the dome and covers less of it. lit_contrast, sun_gain and edge_softness are unchanged: those are what give a cloud a lit top and a shaded base, and they were the half of round 1 that worked.

cloud_sea._comment: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C4), read by cloudreach_world.gd::_build_cloud_decks. The realm already had a CloudSea plane, but it is pinned at world_bounds.min_y+18 = -182 because cloudreach_world_runtime.gd measures the fall-recovery kill plane off that node's own Y -- so it is 340-1340 m under every authored stand and reads exactly as the blind judge described it: 'the gap below it is a featureless grey-blue band, no valley floor, no cloud, no depth'. That plane is untouched. This is a SECOND layer whose height at every cell is the local region tier (interpolated from cloudreach_world.json's own six region crowns by z) minus drop_below_tier_m, then clamped under any walkable surface ground_height_at already knows about -- so it is always a few hundred metres below the player and can never become a ceiling over a lower stand, which a single flat deck at one height would be. lower_deck_offset_m adds a second, bluer sheet further down for a layered depth cue; set it to 0 for one sheet. billow_count 0 disables the cumulus tops and leaves the bare sheets.
cloud_sea._comment_round3: Round 3, off the round-2 judge: the sheet WAS in frame and the judge still reported 'no haze band, no atmospheric layering, no cloud sea'. The layer was not missing, it had no value separation -- an unshaded #c4d5e0 sheet under a hazed pale sky is the same value as the sky, so it read as more sky. A cloud sea reads because its body is DARKER than the sky and only its lit tops are bright, so the sheets go down a full step in value and the billows go fully lit with no emission floor at all. Same reasoning for the two haze tiers: a distant ridge has to be a silhouette against the sky, not a wash in it. drop_below_tier_m 250 -> 190 brings the layer up so more of it falls inside the frame under a rim; the probe had 195 m of worst-case clearance at stand 01 to spend, and min_clearance_m still guards the walkable clamp independently.

distant_relief._comment: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C4), read by cloudreach_world.gd::_build_distant_relief. horizon_ranges below already puts ten ranges on the skyline, but every one of them is a peak ABOVE the player -- which is why the judge read stand 08 as 'the world ends at a hard grey haze line behind the cottages, reading as a sea or a void' and stand 04 as 'a razor-straight terrain edge with sky under it, nothing beyond'. These are wide, low masses out past the realm footprint whose tops sit BELOW the local tier, so a stand on a rim looks down onto them, and the cloud sheet runs between, so they emerge through cloud the way the key art's far ridges do. haze_near/haze_far are the aerial-perspective tiers (judge defect 13, 'far cliffs are as saturated and contrasty as near ones'); range_material names which tier the existing horizon_ranges wear. Set enabled false to remove the lower relief and revert horizon_ranges to the near cliff shader.

island_roots._comment: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C5), read by cloudreach_world.gd::_mesa. The blind judge on stands 04 and 11: 'A detached chunk of cliff hangs in the sky with pebbles falling from it ... it has no underside, no roots, no mist, no anchor -- it reads as a mesh that lost its parent and is a bug to any player who sees it.' Three literal causes, all fixed against this block: _mesa closes its crown and its four wall bands but never capped the bottom ring, so an airborne LandmarkLedge is an open-ended tube; _build_embedded_rock_shelves placed outcrops up to 97 m below a 72 m mass's own crown, i.e. hanging in the air under it, which is the falling pebbles; and nothing marked the base as high air. A mass counts as airborne when its base sits more than airborne_gap_m above landmass.geology_base_y -- every region CliffMass is built down TO that datum and so never qualifies, which is what keeps this off the buried masses where it would be invisible cost.

arrival_beats.description: The weathered marker overlooks the sheltered road toward Galefoot Waycamp. Cloudberries and wind-bent fiber grow along its planted margins.

geology._comment: CLIFF-ART-0906, owner picked option A (2026-09-06). CLIFF-ART-0906 option A: material only. The key art's cliff/stronghold stone is grey-green granite (judge measured RGB 80/79/71 on the board's cut stone) with mossy shelves; the shipped defaults are tan (0.63,0.53,0.40) with ochre strata. Same Rock030 texture, retinted. Every key here maps 1:1 onto a shaders/cloudreach_cliff.gdshader uniform via cloudreach_world.gd::_build_materials; the shader's own defaults are the old tan look, so removing a key reverts that one uniform and removing the block reverts the whole cliff. Rendered options and the judge sheet: ralph/reports/CLIFF-ART-0906/.
geology._comment_normal_scale_atmos0906: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906. NOT part of option A's palette -- no colour here is touched. texture_scale 0.055 is one texture repeat every ~18 m, which is right for the broad albedo planes option A was picked for and badly wrong for the normal map: across a 46 m landmark ledge it stretches one rock normal over the whole face, and the blind judge read the result on the stand-11 spire as 'a dozen bright white-cyan curved scratch lines, swirling across the rock face like chalk ... a UV smear'. normal_scale gives the normal its own frequency (~4.5 m per repeat). Remove the key and the shader falls back to texture_scale, i.e. exactly the shipped look.

crown_relief._comment: OWNER 2026-09-06: 'that completely flat green ground shouldn't exist'. Only a CliffMass got an eroded crown, and even that reached its first contour in ONE triangle per side -- three vertices describe a plane, so every crown rendered as a flat disc however much height the model carried. cloudreach_world.gd now (a) carries relief in the shared height model (_crown_height_at, which the visible crown, its collision copy and every conforming shoulder all read) and (b) subdivides the crown bands so the mesh can show it. amplitude_m is measured at reference_radius_m and scales down with the crown's own radius, so a landing pad still reads as a pad; crowns under min_radius_m are left alone. The relief zeroes itself inside a settlement clearance and within LINE_PIN_MARGIN_M+LINE_EASE_M of any road or bridge deck -- without that it would roll through an authored ribbon and reopen the hole/sink class OP-0905-24/25 closed. mesh_step_m is the target quad size of the subdivision and is the cheap lever if triangle count matters.
crown_relief._comment_terrace_atmos0906: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C3). The waves above give a crown texture; they do not give it structure, and the blind judge's first defect was 'there is no vertical in this cliff region ... nothing looks down'. terrace_drop_m/bench_count step a crown DOWN from its centre to its rim in broad benches with walkable risers, through the same shared height model the waves use -- so the visible crown, its collision copy and every conforming shoulder move together. The sign is negative on purpose: _surfaces registers a region as one ellipse at its authored top and ground_height_at answers that flat number for the whole disc, so a crown that rose above it would spawn a loaded player inside a hill. terrace_line_ease_m is the terrace's own, much wider road suppression -- 15 m of drop recovered over the waves' 6 m LINE_EASE_M would be a wall across a ribbon's shoulder. min_radius_m dropped 40 -> 28 so the rugged spur crowns that flank every road (crown span 31-43 m) are shaped too; a LandmarkLedge (span 20.7 m), a transition ledge (20 m) and every landing pad stay under it and are untouched.

landmass._comment_route_edge_drop_atmos0906: CLOUDREACH-ATMOS-0906 (C3). _route_ridge drops each shoulder's OUTER edge below the crest before the cliff wall hangs off it. At the shipped 4-22 m that is a rolled grassy shoulder, not an edge -- and the stands the brief names for standing on an edge (the arrival reveal, the causeway) sit on route shoulders BETWEEN regions, so the crown terraces never reach them. 14-54 m makes it a lip a player can look over. It is emitted into the same station vertices the walkable rows, the wall attachment and the collision copy are all built from, so the render and the collider move together; ground truth was re-run across this change. Set both back to 4.0/9.0 to revert exactly.

route_details._comment: Individually authored roadside pockets. Offsets are [sideways, forward] metres from each anchor; dimensions are actual final mesh bounds. Keep the route centre free and never bridge a missing surface with dressing.

pockets._comment_dress_0906: CLOUDREACH-DRESS-0906 / C7 follow-up. The blind judge on the summit approach: 'To its right a bare lumber stack and a plank shed sit half over the edge of the plateau.' Probed from the stand-06 camera (tools/_probe_cloudreach_dark_props.gd -- --stand=06), the object filling that rectangle is THIS pocket's wagon -- Prop_Wagon, 24 m from the lens, spanning screen x 795-1049 -- with the fence panel beside it reading as the shed. It is not the stronghold's own approach props, which were a separate instance of the same mistake and were fixed alongside it. The four man-made items move ~3 m inward off the lip, gain a paving apron so they sit on something, and are joined by a workbench, a bag and a second crate so the group reads as a supply post somebody uses rather than as lumber tipped over the edge. The rock/bush/flower items on the +x side are unchanged.
